sections.title: Overview of Transportation Management
sections.text:
4.1 Overview of Transportation Management
Systems
A transportation management system is a software platform that the
transportation industry employs to plan, execute, and optimize the movements
of goods, including both inbound and outbound shipments. A transportation
management system ensures compliance with regulations and furnishes the
necessary documentation. Managing transportation can be complex, expensive,
and time consuming, and thus, a transportation management system is a crucial
tool for streamlining supply chains. Transportation was once viewed as a distinct
business process, but now it is integrated into overall supply chain and logistics
management. A transportation management system frequently forms part of a
larger supply chain management system.
To deal with the growing complexity and uncertainty of global logistics,
businesses must improve logistics processes, enhance services, and increase
visibility and control.
A transportation management system provides a holistic perspective of daily
transportation operations, encompassing trade compliance data, essential
documentation, and the timely delivery of goods and freight. Transportation
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

230
management system solutions streamline shipping processes, allowing an
enterprise to oversee and enhance its transportation operations across various
modes of transportation, such as land, air, and sea.
Transportation management systems play a crucial role in modern supply
chains, affecting each stage of the process, from planning and procurement to
logistics and lifecycle management. A strong transportation management
system offers comprehensive visibility, facilitating more effective transportation
planning and execution, leading to improved customer satisfaction and
increased sales growth. Given the continuously changing global trade
environment, having a transportation management system that can assist
businesses in successfully navigating complex trade policies and guaranteeing
compliance with regulations is vital.
Transportation management systems are primarily employed by businesses that
require frequent shipping, moving, and receiving services, such as
manufacturers, distributors, e-commerce companies, and retail businesses.
Additionally, logistics service providers, including third-party logistics (3PL) and
fourth-party logistics (4PL) firms, commonly use transportation management
systems to provide logistics services to their clients.
The SAP TM application integrates fleet management and logistics
management, streamlining the movement of goods across various modes of
transportation. In this way, SAP TM enhances operational efficiency and reduces
costs.
This solution offers a range of features, including transportation demand
management, order consolidation, shipment monitoring and tracking, and
transportation spend optimization. Additionally, it facilitates strategic freight
procurement, capacity monitoring, freight order management, and
transportation planning optimization. Furthermore, SAP TM assists in the
management of freight financials through freight settlement and provides
analysis and reporting capabilities to make informed transportation decisions.
Employing SAP TM, enterprises can implement a uniform transportation system
that results in decreased transportation expenses and increased customer
contentment. This software streamlines transportation planning, execution, and
cost reconciliation, while also furnishing valuable data analytics to augment the
overall transportation process.
As shown in Figure 4.1, SAP TM, when used in conjunction with SAP S/4HANA,
can be deployed in a variety of deployment and integration scenarios.
© 

231
Figure 4.1 SAP TM Deployment Options
The following list describes these options in more detail:
Internal system or embedded integration
In this first scenario, referred to as internal system integration or embedded
integration, SAP TM is directly integrated into the SAP S/4HANA system
instance. In this approach, SAP TM can directly access logistics data within the
SAP S/4HANA system, thus eliminating the need for data transfers between
the systems. This approach eliminates the possibility of redundant data and
reduces the effort required for data transfer.
External system or side-by-side integration
In this second scenario, referred to as external system integration or side-by-
side integration, SAP TM is implemented as a separate system. In this
approach, master data and transactional data are transmitted from the SAP
S/4HANA or SAP ERP system to SAP TM using various techniques for
replicating master data.
SAP TM, which is a component of SAP S/4HANA, can function as a standalone
system in side-by-side scenarios in the following ways:
SAP TM can be integrated with existing enterprise resource planning (ERP)
instances that have not yet been converted to SAP S/4HANA, as part of the
SAP S/4HANA system.
In situations with multiple SAP S/4HANA instances in a system landscape,
SAP TM can be integrated with each instance.
SAP TM can be implemented with support packs and released
independently of other SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management applications
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

232
to accommodate different software lifecycle management requirements.
While this option may result in a higher total cost of ownership (TCO), the
trade-off might be necessary.
Note
Note that, for additional information on deployment and integration options,
we recommend consulting the following SAP Notes:
2714892 - SAP Transportation Management - Deployment Options
2812981 - Transportation Management and decentralized EWM in same SAP
S/4HANA system and client
Integration options between SAP EWM and SAP TM
Different integration options between SAP EWM and SAP TM are available,
such as the following:
Direct integration of embedded EWM and embedded SAP TM on SAP
S/4HANA
As shown in Figure 4.2, the SAP S/4HANA platform presents a seamless
fusion of embedded EWM and embedded SAP TM modules. This
amalgamation facilitates instantaneous communications between the two
modules and enables a comprehensive look at logistics operations. By
virtue of this direct integration, SAP EWM and SAP TM leverage a unified
database, effectively eliminating data redundancy and ensuring data
coherence.
Figure 4.2 Direct Integration of Embedded EWM and Embedded SAP TM
Integrate decentralized Extended Warehouse Management in SAP
S/4HANA (decentralized EWM) and standalone SAP TM
As shown in Figure 4.3, SAP S/4HANA provides a streamlined solution for
integrating your decentralized EWM and standalone SAP TM modules. This
© 

233
approach allows for enhanced supply chain management capabilities,
enabling your organization to efficiently oversee the flow of goods and
optimize logistics processes.
Figure 4.3 Integrate Decentralized EWM and Standalone SAP TM
Integrate decentralized EWM on SAP S/4HANA and embedded SAP TM
on SAP S/4HANA and embedded SAP TM on SAP S/4HANA
As shown in Figure 4.4, SAP S/4HANA provides seamless integration
between a decentralized EWM system and the embedded SAP TM modules.
Figure 4.4 Integrate Decentralized EWM and Embedded SAP TM
Indirectly integrate SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP or SAP
S/4HANA
As shown in Figure 4.5, in this particular scenario, the SAP EWM and SAP TM
systems can be integrated with SAP ERP, and the exchange of data between
these systems is facilitated through the SAP ERP system.

234
Figure 4.5 Indirect Integration SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP
Several benefits of this indirect integration approach include the following:
Leveraging existing SAP ERP infrastructure and investments: By
integrating SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP, a business can make the
most of its existing infrastructure and investment in SAP ERP systems.
This approach can reduce the cost and effort required to deploy and
maintain separate systems for warehouse management and
transportation management.
Streamlined data flow between SAP EWM, SAP TM, and other ERP
modules: Indirect integration between SAP EWM, SAP TM, and other ERP
modules, such as sales, procurement, and inventory management, can
help streamline data flows across different business functions. This
approach can lead to improved data accuracy, better decision-making,
and reduced errors.
Improved visibility and control over end-to-end supply chain processes:
By integrating SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP, a business can gain
better visibility and control over its supply chain processes. This
approach can help identify and address issues quickly, optimize
operations, and improve customer satisfaction.
Management of transportation planning and execution within the
context of broader business processes: Integrating SAP EWM and SAP TM
with SAP ERP can help a business manage transportation planning and
execution within the context of broader business processes, such as
order fulfillment and inventory management. This approach can help
ensure that transportation plans are aligned with broader business goals
and objectives.
© 

235
Reduced manual effort and increased efficiency through automation:
Indirect integration between SAP EWM, SAP TM, and SAP ERP can help
reduce manual effort and increase efficiency through automation. This
approach can lead to faster processing times, reduced errors, and
improved productivity.

4.2 Shipping and Receiving in Inbound and
Outbound Processes
Shipping and receiving in inbound and outbound processes in SAP EWM are
essential components of warehouse management systems. SAP EWM
streamlines shipping and receiving processes, providing real-time visibility,
efficient order processing, and enhanced inventory control. By automating and
optimizing these processes, a business can improve in overall warehouse
efficiency, can reduce errors, and can enhance customer satisfaction.
SAP provides a range of business processes aimed at facilitating seamless
integration between transportation management processes and warehouse
management processes, with the ultimate goal of meeting customer
requirements. These processes are designed to ensure the smooth management
of inbound and outbound shipments, as well as the efficient use of transportation
units (TUs) and vehicles within a warehouse.
The shipping and receiving aspects of EWM encompass the following key areas:
Utilization of vehicles and TUs to manage goods transport to and from the
warehouse
Loading and unloading operations, including docking and undocking
procedures at warehouse doors
Yard management, which involves the organization and optimization of
warehouse yard space
Regarding inbound and outbound processes, shipping and receiving processes
play a vital role in efficiently planning and executing warehouse activities. By
leveraging these processes, your business can effectively manage the flow of
goods, handle incoming shipments, and ensure timely and accurate deliveries to
customers or other destinations. The integration of shipping and receiving
functionalities in both inbound and outbound operations enhances overall
warehouse efficiency, inventory control, and customer satisfaction as well as
enable the following capabilities:
Integration of freight orders in SAP TM (processes based on freight order
integration in SAP TM)
© 

237
This process involves linking SAP TM with SAP EWM to manage inbound and
outbound shipments.
Use of vehicles and TUs and TUs in SAP EWM (processes based on use of
vehicles and TUs in SAP EWM)
This process entails integrating SAP EWM with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to
manage TUs and vehicles within the warehouse.
Shipment integration in SAP ERP (processes based on use of shipment
integration in SAP ERP)
This process involves connecting SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA with SAP EWM to
oversee shipments and related processes.
Shipment integration in SAP ERP and SAP TM (processes based on use of
shipment and integration in SAP ERP and SAP TM)
This process involves integrating SAP TM and SAP EWM with SAP ERP or SAP
S/4HANA to oversee shipments throughout the transportation and warehouse
management process as a whole.
In summary, SAP offers various business processes that support the integration
of transportation management and warehouse management processes to
enable a seamless experience for users and customers.

sections.title: Freight Order Integration
sections.text:
4.3 Freight Order Integration
For inbound goods receipts as well as outbound goods issues, transportation
planning is performed in SAP TM based on purchase orders, deliveries, sales
orders, or customer return orders in SAP ERP. SAP TM sends planned freight
order data directly to SAP EWM, which converts the information from the freight
order into planned shipping and receiving activities in SAP EWM, namely,
activities involving vehicles or TUs. You can perform all warehouse activities,
such as loading or unloading, and perform goods receipts or goods issues for all
deliveries.

sections.title: Inbound Process
sections.text:
4.3.1 Inbound Process
In this section, we’ll go through the inbound goods receipt process using freight
order integration in SAP TM. We’ll explore transportation planning based on
purchase orders in the following sections.
Business Process
Figure 4.6 shows the step-by-step process for inbound goods receipt, which is
performed in the following sequence:
1. Purchase orders are received by SAP TM from either SAP ERP or SAP
S/4HANA, and their corresponding transportation requirements and freight
units are generated.
2. Transportation planning is carried out based on transportation
requirements, and freight orders are created in SAP TM.
3. If transportation planning is based on purchase orders, SAP TM generates
deliveries in either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA.
4. Inbound deliveries are then distributed by SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP
EWM, which automatically generates corresponding warehouse requests.
5. Freight order information is sent by SAP TM to SAP EWM, which
automatically creates planned shipping and receiving activities for the
assigned vehicle or TU. Inbound deliveries are also assigned to the created
TU activities.
© 

239
6. The system automatically changes the status of the shipping and receiving
activity from Planned to Active when a warehouse operator or checkpoint
clerk executes the arrival at checkpoint action for the vehicle or TU.
7. An operator or goods receipt clerk then assigns a door to the vehicle or TU.
If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to
the assigned door; if not, the Arrival at Door action is executed for the
vehicle or TU.
8. Warehouse activities, such as unloading goods, posting goods receipts, and
putting away goods, are then carried out.
9. If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to
the yard; if not, the Departure from Door action is executed for the vehicle
or TU.
10. The operator executes the Departure from Checkpoint action for the vehicle
or TUs, and SAP EWM automatically changes the status of the shipping and
receiving activity from Active to Completed. This action triggers a
notification to SAP TM about the executed shipping and receiving activities
for the vehicle or TU, and the freight order is updated accordingly.
11. The SAP TM freight order’s execution status is then set to Completed.
12. Freight settlement is carried out in SAP TM, and the freight settlement
document serves as the basis for invoice verification and settlement in SAP
ERP.
Figure 4.6 Freight Order Integration in SAP TM and SAP EWM: Inbound Process
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

240
Configuration
In this section, we’ll explore the key configuration steps needed for this process,
assuming that the primary SAP EWM customization settings are already

1. Define control keys for document integration
You define control keys that specify which documents in a document chain
are to be integrated into SAP TM. You can define as many control keys as

a control key for document integration will be defined. Follow the IMG
menu path Integration with Other SAP Components • Transportation
Management • Logistics Integration • Define Control Key for Document
Integration. To define a control key for document integration, click New
Entries and maintain control key parameters. If you’re using order-based
planning, make sure the PO to TM checkbox is activated, as shown in
Figure 4.7.
Figure 4.7 Control Key Parameters
2. Define a logistic integration profile
You can control settings for the building of freight units when working with
the internal SAP TM component. You can create and assign profiles to SAP
TM-relevant business document types. In this setting, a logistics integration
profile and corresponding freight order building rule will be defined. Follow
the IMG menu path Transportation Management • Logistics Integration •
Internal TM Component Integration • Define Logistics Integration
Profile. To define logistic integration profiles, click New Entries and
configure logistics integration profile Y002 and maintain other details, as
shown in Figure 4.8. Alternatively, you can verify that standard SAP
configuration settings on this screen meet your business requirements.
© 

241
3. Define the transport-relevance of purchasing documents
You can activate the integration of purchase orders into SAP TM by
assigning a control key to the required purchase order. In this setting,
transport-relevant purchasing document setting will be defined. Follow the
IMG menu path Transportation Management • Logistics Integration •
Internal TM Component Integration • Define Transportation-Relevance
of Purchasing Documents. To define transportation-relevant purchasing
documents, click New Entries and configure transport-relevant purchasing
document settings for control key 0055 and with logistics integration profile
Y002 (Log Int. Profile) as shown in Figure 4.9. Alternatively, you can verify
that standard SAP configuration settings on this screen meet your business
requirements..
Figure 4.8 Logistics Integration Profile
Figure 4.9 Transport-Relevant Purchasing Document
4. Define the transport relevance of delivery documents
You activate the integration of inbound deliveries into SAP TM by assigning
a control key to the required inbound delivery. In this setting, the transport-
relevant delivery document setting will be defined. Follow the IMG menu
path Transportation Management • Logistics Integration • Internal TM
Component Integration • Define Transportation-Relevance of Delivery
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

242
Documents. Click New Entries and configure transport-relevant delivery
document settings for control key 0056 (Control Key), logistics integration
profile Y002 (Log. Int. Profile), and delivery type EL (Del. Type), as shown
in Figure 4.10. Alternatively, you can verify that standard SAP configuration

Figure 4.10 Transport-Relevant Delivery Document
5. Create a freight unit building rule
In this SAP NetWeaver setting, a freight unit building rule will be defined.
Follow the SAP NetWeaver menu path Application • Administration •
Planning • General Planning Settings • Freight Unit Building Rule •
Create Freight Unit Building Rule. As shown in Figure 4.11, verify that
Document Type 0001 has been maintained and the value in the Critical

6. Define freight order types
Freight orders are created as the result of planning, especially in land
transportation, and the freight bookings are used in air or sea
transportation. In a subcontracting process, a freight order is the
transportation document that is sent to the carrier once assigned via carrier
selection or tendering. Follow the IMG menu path Transportation
Management • Freight Order Management • Freight Order • Define
Freight Order Types. To define a freight order type, click New Entries and
configure freight order settings, as shown in Figure 4.12. Enter “2000” into
the EWM Integration Profile field and “1000” into the Freight Order Type
field.
© 

243
Figure 4.11 Display Freight Unit Building Rule
Figure 4.12 Freight Order Type
7. Define an SAP EWM integration profile
You can define a profile for direct integration with SAP EWM or an external
warehouse management system. In this setting, SAP EWM integration

Management • Define EWM Integration Profile. Click New Entries and

sending loading and unloading instructions in the Settings for Inbound
and Settings for Outbound Stop.
Figure 4.13 SAP EWM Integration Profile
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

244
8. Activate the action definition in the PPF
In this setting, transportation management relevance action definition will
be activated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse

Settings • Shipping and Receiving • Message Processing • Define Action

Figure 4.14 Activate Action Definition for TU
Master Data Setup
Let’s go through the important master data settings needed for inbound goods
receipt processes next:
1. Location master : assign warehouse number and target system
In this master data setup, location-related settings will be performed. The

Transaction /SCMTMS/LOC3. To assign a warehouse number and logical
system to a location master in SAP EWM, enter the Location and maintain
the SAP EWM Warehouse Number and SAP EWM Target System fields, as
shown in Figure 4.15.
© 

245
Figure 4.15 Display Location: Assign Warehouse
2. Assign packaging material to SAP TM means of transport
In this master data, the packaging material is assigned to an SAP TM means
of transport for a location. Follow the menu path Logistics • SCM Extended
Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Settings
• Shipping and Receiving • Link between Packaging Material (TU) and

Figure 4.16 Link between Packaging Material and Means of Transport
Process Demo

1. Create a purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA

sections.title: Outbound Process
sections.text:
4.3.2 Outbound Process
Throughout this section, we’ll provide a comprehensive overview of the
outbound goods issue process and the integration of freight orders in SAP TM.
We’ll also delve into transportation planning based on sales orders in detail.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 4.31, the step-by-step process for outbound processes
involves the following sequence:
1. A sales order is created in SAP SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA.
2. SAP TM receives orders and deliveries from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and
utilizes the information to create transportation requirements and freight
units.
3. After establishing the transportation requirements, SAP TM performs
transportation planning and generates freight orders.
4. If the transportation planning is based on sales orders, SAP TM generates
deliveries in the ERP system. These outbound deliveries are then
forwarded to SAP EWM, which automatically generates the corresponding
warehouse requests of the outbound delivery order type.
5. Based on the freight orders, SAP TM sends a loading appointment request
message to SAP EWM, which creates a vehicle or TU along with planned
shipping and receiving activities.
© 

253
6. The outbound delivery orders are assigned to TU activities. Warehouse
activities, such as picking, packing, staging, and loading of goods, can be
performed before the vehicle or TU arrives at the door.
7. When the vehicle or TU arrives, the Arrival at Checkpoint action is
executed, and the system changes the status of the shipping and receiving
activity from Planned to Active. A door is then assigned to the vehicle or
TU, and if yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the
yard to the assigned door.
8. Once the warehouse activities are finished, the goods issue is posted, and
transportation documents are printed. The delivery information is
transferred to SAP ERP, where the deliveries are automatically updated
with execution data. The information is also sent to SAP TM to update the
consumed transportation requirements.
9. If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to
the yard, and if not, the Departure from Door action is executed. When the
Departure from Checkpoint action is executed, SAP EWM automatically
changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Active to
Completed.
10. A loading appointment notification message is then transmitted to SAP
TM, where the freight orders are updated with execution data. The
execution status of the SAP TM freight order is set to Completed, and
freight settlement is conducted in SAP TM. The freight settlement
document in SAP TM serves as the foundation for invoice verification and
settlement in the ERP system.
Figure 4.31 Freight Order Integration in SAP TM and SAP EWM: Outbound Process
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

254
Configuration
In this section, we’ll explore the key configuration options needed for this
process, assuming that the primary SAP EWM customization settings are already
configured in the system:
1. Define control keys for document integration
You define control keys that determine which documents in a document
chain should be integrated into SAP TM. You can define as many control
keys as required, with different combinations of relevant documents.
Follow the IMG menu path Integration with Other SAP Components •
Transportation Management • Logistics Integration • Define Control Key
for Document Integration. Click New Entries and maintain control key
parameters. If you’re using order-based planning, make sure the SO to TM
checkbox is activated, as shown in Figure 4.32.
Figure 4.32 Control Key Parameter
2. Define a logistics integration profile
You can control settings for the building of freight units when working with
the internal SAP TM component. You can create and assign profiles to SAP
TM-relevant business document types. In this setting, a logistics integration
profile and corresponding freight order building rule will be defined. Follow
the IMG menu path Transportation Management • Integration • Logistics
Integration • Internal TM Component Integration • Define Logistics
Integration Profile. To define a logistics integration profile, click New
Entries and configure logistics integration profile Y001, as shown in
Figure 4.33.
© 

255
Figure 4.33 Logistics Integration Profile
3. Define the transport relevance of sales documents
You can activate the integration of sales orders into SAP TM by assigning a
control key to the required sales order. In this step, the transport-relevant
sales document setting will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path
Transportation Management • Integration • Logistics Integration •

sections.title: Advanced Shipping and Receiving
sections.text:
4.4 Advanced Shipping and Receiving
Advanced shipping and receiving empowers individuals to efficiently send,
receive, and transport goods through a comprehensive and seamless procedure.
It streamlines the process from the moment a truck arrives at the gate to the
ultimate receipt of goods in the warehouse by enabling mixed and multi-
warehouse scenarios to be managed within a single freight order. This system
allows a truck that has registered its arrival at a checkpoint to perform loading
and unloading operations at a single location or to distribute goods to multiple
warehouses at the same site.
To create transportation requirements, both materials management and sales
and distribution must be in place, and information exchange among various SAP
S/4HANA application components, such as SAP TM, SAP EWM, stock room
management, inventory management and physical inventory, and logistics
execution is streamlined through the utilization of a unified data model. The
application of the EDIFACT standard to electronic data interchange (EDI)
messages and the provision of specialized applications further simplify the
exchange of information. Additionally, existing apps and RF transactions for
shipping and receiving processes are expanded to facilitate communication,
allowing users to track the status of products throughout the shipping and
receiving processes and gain valuable insights.
The advanced shipping and receiving process is based on the freight order and
does not utilize either the TUs or vehicles in SAP EWM.

As shown in Figure 4.51, the inbound goods receipt process involves the

1. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA generates a purchase order.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

5. Once the inbound delivery is dispatched from SAP S/4HANA, it is created in

4.4.2 Outbound Process
The Advanced Shipping and Receiving outbound process in SAP EWM
commences with sales, followed by transportation planning and warehouse
processing, and concludes with the departure of the truck from the warehouse.
We’ll walk through this process in detail in the following sections.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

276
Business Process
As shown in Figure 4.76, the outbound delivery process with advanced shipping
notifications (ASNs) involves the following steps:
1. To initiate the outbound process in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, a sales
document such as a sales order or scheduling agreement is generated. This
triggers the creation of freight Units for order-based planning, which are
then replicated to Transportation Management.
2. In SAP TM, freight orders are created for the freight units and outbound
deliveries are generated. These outbound deliveries are replicated to SAP
ERP or SAP S/4HANA as well as to SAP EWM.
3. The pick, pack, and stage processes for the outbound delivery order are
executed in the embedded EWM system.
4. Once the freight order is marked as Ready for Transportation Execution
and the outbound delivery orders are marked as Ready for Shipping, the
loading process can be initiated in SAP EWM via the Load or Unload Freight
Orders app or an RF device.
5. Using the Load or Unload Freight Orders app in SAP Fiori, door assignment,
loading, loading completion, and goods movements can be posted on the
outbound delivery order. The goods movement can be posted either in SAP
TM or SAP EWM.

sections.title: Shipment Integration

4.5 Shipment Integration
To transport multiple outbound delivery documents using the same means of
transportation, SAP ERP utilizes shipment documents as a foundation for
planning the logistics. The system converts handling units (HUs) within SAP ERP
shipments into vehicles, TUs, or both, and schedules shipping and receiving
activities in SAP EWM. Following the completion of the warehouse operations,
transport details are transmitted back to SAP ERP to facilitate freight cost
settlement and invoicing.

4.5.1 Transportation Planning in an ERP System
In this section, we’ll explore the outbound transportation planning process in
your ERP system followed by the execution of warehouse activities in SAP EWM.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 4.103, the outbound process involves the following steps:
1. In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, an outbound delivery (with reference to a sales
order) is created. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA automatically distributes
outbound deliveries to SAP EWM, where warehouse requests for outbound
deliveries are generated.
2. To create a shipment with HUs and assign outbound deliveries, you can use
SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The shipment details are then sent to SAP EWM,
where a vehicle or TU and a planned shipping and receiving activity are
automatically created, and the outbound delivery order is assigned to the
TU activity.
3. Warehouse activities related to outbound delivery orders, such as picking,
packing, staging, and loading the goods, are carried out in SAP EWM.
4. To activate the shipping and receiving activity from Planned to Active, you
need to execute the Arrival at Checkpoint action for the vehicle or TU. Then,
you can assign a door to the vehicle or TU.
5. If yard management is enabled, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to
the assigned door. However, if yard management is not activated, the
© 

291
Arrival at Door action for the vehicle or TU is executed.
6. When the goods issue posting takes place in SAP EWM, the transport details
are transferred to SAP ERP, where a shipment is automatically updated with
the execution data.
7. If yard management is enabled, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to
the yard. Conversely, if yard management is not activated, the Departure
from Door action for the vehicle or TU is executed.

4.5.2 Transportation Planning in SAP EWM
In a scenario driven by SAP EWM, also referred to as SAP EWM-based
transportation planning, transportation planning is performed by the SAP EWM
system itself. This is achieved by creating a TU and assigning the unit to delivery.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 4.129, the outbound process with transportation planning in
SAP EWM involves the following steps:
1. To begin, create an outbound delivery in either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
and reference the sales order.
2. The system will automatically replicate the outbound delivery to SAP EWM
and block its execution until planning results become available. The
delivery item screen will display the DBT - Blocked (Transp. Plan) status
type, indicating that SAP EWM is responsible for transportation planning.
The Transportation Planning Type field in the delivery screen will have the
value B - Obligatory External Planning in SAP EWM.
3. In SAP EWM, create a TU activity and assign the outbound delivery order.
The system will update the delivery header’s transportation data from TU,
such as the means of transport and vehicle. The outbound delivery order
© 

305
can now be executed, and its DBT - Blocked (Transp. Plan) status will no
longer be set.
4. Create a warehouse task in SAP EWM for the outbound delivery order to
move the product from a storage bin to the staging area. A warehouse order
will be generated for the delivery order, and a pick-HU will be created for
the warehouse task. The pick HU will be utilized as the destination HU.
5. Confirm the warehouse task in SAP EWM to move the product to the staging
area for the outbound delivery order.
6. Once the TU arrives at the checkpoint in SAP EWM, the TU status will change
to Activated.
7. In SAP EWM, move the TU from the checkpoint to the door.
8. Perform loading and post goods issue in SAP EWM.
9. After the goods issue has been posted, the system will replicate it from SAP
EWM to SAP ERP and create an entry in the document flow of the outbound
delivery in SAP ERP.
10. In SAP ERP, create and display a shipment and assign the outbound
delivery. The system will send the SHPMNT05 IDoc from SAP EWM to SAP
ERP, which will create an SAP ERP shipment with the assigned delivery. The
new shipment will be displayed for the delivery, and the goods issue status
on the header and item level will be set to Complete. The overall status of
the shipment will be Planning Completed.
11. In SAP EWM, move the TU from the door back to the checkpoint.
12. Once the TU departs from the checkpoint in SAP EWM, the process is
complete.

5 Dock Appointment Scheduling
Dock appointment scheduling is a proactive and anticipatory planning
technique employed by companies to manage shipping docks, warehouses,
and distribution centers. This method entails the allocation of designated
time slots for the arrival and departure of trucks transporting inbound and
outbound shipments. Moreover, the optimization of schedules for dock
doors and yard operations is an integral aspect of dock scheduling. The
objective of this chapter is to serve as a comprehensive manual on diverse
dock management procedures and their seamless assimilation with SAP
Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) through embedded Extended
Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM). We’ll walk
through the business processes for each technique, discuss the setup and
primary data requirements needed to enable end-to-end testing of business
scenarios, and provide a complete step-by-step process demonstration for
each scenario.
The integration of SAP with SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling presents a
synergistic opportunity for warehouse and distribution centers to streamline
and optimize their goods flow. The process entails configuring and linking the
dock appointment scheduling system with SAP EWM’s inbound and outbound
delivery procedures.
At the outset, the SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling system meticulously
schedules precise time slots for the arrival and departure of trucks that ferry
inbound and outbound shipments. Subsequently, this scheduling information is
conveyed to SAP EWM, which then triggers the generation of inbound or
outbound deliveries based on the designated time slots. Following the creation
of the inbound or outbound delivery in SAP EWM, the system automatically
assigns a specific dock door for the truck to utilize, based on the schedule
information retrieved from SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. This approach
ensures the accurate routing of trucks to designated dock doors, thereby
optimizing the flow of goods. In sum, the integration of SAP Dock Appointment
